elements.evidence: "Customer may solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee" (replacing "Customer shall not solicit")
"may solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee" — the hire/employ prohibition is removed
"during the term or for twenty-four months afterward" struck from the operative text
Clause now runs only one way as a permission to Customer; no Vendor-side obligation created

elements.evidence: "may solicit, hire, or employ" — no hiring prohibition remains

reasons: The locked preferred level is fully achieved: the prohibition on soliciting, hiring, or employing Vendor employees and the 24-month post-term tail are both eliminated, so no non-solicit or no-hire binds Customer.

The edit is a minimal operator flip ("shall not" → "may") plus deletion of the duration phrase; no new exception, obligation, or boilerplate was introduced and the deterministic minimality gate passes.

Fallback elements (mutuality, service-personnel scope, 12-month period, advertisement/unsolicited-approach carve-outs) are absent, but that is expected and permissible because preferred and fallback are separate bargains and preferred was targeted and met; the failed official duration and carve-out checks are therefore not defects here.

Drafting nit only: the retained trailing phrase "regardless of how the employee applies" is a harmless remnant that now qualifies a permission rather than a prohibition; consider deleting it for cleanliness, but it creates no undefined term or contradiction.
Margin comment correctly states the position and offers the fallback without lecturing; nothing in it is relied on operatively.
